 October 29, 2026 at 5:00 am CDT Expand Northern Illinois University's wide receiver DeAree Rogers (1) catches a pass while being defended by Hawaii’s Elijah Palmer during the game on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026, held at Huskie Stadium in DeKalb. (David Toney for Shaw Local News /David Toney)
 Buy Photo
 By Eddie Carifio 
 The NIU football team heads to Las Vegas on Saturday, facing UNLV for the fifth time and the first since 2015.
 NIU (0-7 overall, 0-3 Mountain West) has won all five meetings between the two programs, the most recent a 38-30 win in DeKalb in 2015 . Both teams were members of the Big West Conference from 1993 until 1995. The teams met in 1995, with the Huskies winning 62-14 in DeKalb. NIU won 48-34 on its Vegas last trip in 2014.
 The Rebels (4-3, 2-1) had a three-game winning streak snapped last week with a 41-31 loss at Air Force despite leading in the third quarter.
 The Huskies enter the game ranked in the bottom 10 in 16 statistical categories nationally, including six offensive, six defensive and four special teams. They rank 138th, last, in red-zone offense, kickoff-return defense and third-down conversion defense.
 Here’s what to know about the game:
 Johnson still producing despite dismal run-game numbers
 Junior running back Telly Johnson Jr. entered the season with high expectations and was a preseason candidate for the Doak Walker Award. 
 He as rushed for 502 yards and four touchdowns this year. His 5.28 yards per carry rank 50th nationally and fifth in the Mountain West, while his 71.7 yards per game rank 65th in the FBS and sixth in the conference.
 But as a team, the Huskies are 132nd in rushing offense (100.1 yards per game).
 Interim coach Rob Harley said the flavor of the games has a lot to do with that. With the Huskies falling behind, he said, they’ve had to throw the ball more. 
 “We’ve made it an emphasis and we’ve had a chance to go hit some big plays,” Harley said. “It’s there. I don’t know if the numbers are necessarily indicative of what’s going on in the flow. And again, we want to do what works. So I don’t know if it’s necessarily a thought process, more than what’s kind of hot.”
 In the first quarter last week against Hawaii, a 56-21 loss to a Rainbow Warriors team that entered the game with one win and a bottom-10 scoring offense , Johnson ran four times for 3 yards. He finished with 63 yards on 14 carries, his lowest output since a 40-0 season-opening loss at Iowa. 
 Checking something every week, except the final result
 Harley said a lot of what went wrong against Hawaii was anomalies, and the team wasn’t going to spend time chasing ghosts on issues that haven’t been problems all year.
 He mentioned one play where the defense thought it was in a different coverage and left a player uncovered, but didn’t specify the play. He could have been referring to a 62-yard screen pass on third-and-10 from Micah Alejado to Cam Barfield. It was 21-14 at the time, with 6:14 left in the second quarter, but the Rainbow Warriors scored two plays later and led 35-14 at halftime. 
 To reduce those anomalies, Harley said the team is running more good vs. good drills in practices. The coaching staff is decreasing the amount of time spent on scout team drills and instead having the first-team offense go directly against the first-team defense.
 “We’re going to raise the competition in practice and just put them in those situations that are hard to create,” Harley said. “I could do a drill, but I can’t set that up. Those things just naturally pop up when you’re going against each other. So we’re trying to create as many of those organic situations as we can.”
 Harley said the goal isn’t perfection. But when mistakes are made, they cannot be catastrophic. If 75% of the plays are really good and 25% are “eeeh, it’s average,” Harley said the Huskies can play a pretty good game.
 “It seems like every week we’re covering something, we’re checking something off the list,” Harley said. “If we can all do our 1/11th, and do it play in and play out. We know it’s a football game, we know it’s not going to be 100%. But if we can do that, arguably every position group could shine.”
 Falke records fourth interception of season
 Junior Yassine Falke had an interception in each of his first three games but went the next three without one. 
 The game was well out of hand, but Falke came up with his fourth of the season early in the fourth quarter against Alejado. NIU scored a touchdown on the ensuing drive to cut the Hawaii lead to 49-21.
 Falke leads the Mountain West and is third nationally with 0.57 interceptions per game.
 “He just kind of has a knack,” Harley said. “You like to put your most athletic guys and best read-and-react guys to the field, and he’s one of those. He’s found himself near the football and made some big plays.”
